title: Create temporal contrast and kinetic elevation tokens for microinteractions
creator: Ava Martinez
title_long: Introduce small-scale temporal contrast tokens and kinetic elevation token set to improve microinteraction clarity across density modes
description: Add a new family of design tokens that explicitly encode temporal contrast (subtle, transient color/opacity deltas used during hover/press/selected microstates) and kinetic elevation (micro-shadow presets optimized for sub-4px offsets used in fast microinteractions). This ticket covers design definitions, a lightweight Figma spec, recommended CSS/token mappings, and a migration plan for buttons, tables, and chart interactive elements. The goal is to make microinteraction affordances more consistent, easier to audit in the console, and cheaper to render across platforms while preserving accessibility for motion-sensitive and low-vision users.
rationale: Current token set treats interaction states using generic color ramps and large elevation steps which causes small controls (dense tables, compact buttons, sparklines) to either look flat or produce noisy shadows. By defining temporal contrast tokens and kinetic elevation tokens, we can standardize microinteraction feedback, reduce per-component overrides, and provide clear upgrade paths for teams relying on the tokens in console, widgets, and on-prem SDKs.
proposed_tokens: temporal-contrast-xxs: 0.04 alpha overlay (for fastest transient feedback)
temporal-contrast-sm: 0.12 alpha overlay (selected or focused micro state)
token_examples: Buttons (compact): use temporal-contrast-xs on hover + kinetic-elevation-1 for outlineless primary
Table row hover (dense mode): temporal-contrast-xxs background overlay + kinetic-elevation-1 on actionable cell
Chart point focus: temporal-contrast-sm highlight + kinetic-elevation-2 for marker shadow
migration_plan: Phase 1 (Design): finalize token names & numeric scales; publish Figma styles for light/dark variants
Phase 2 (Dev): add tokens to token-variables.json and design-tokens package as non-breaking aliases
Phase 3 (Implement): update Button, TableRow, ChartPoint components to reference new tokens behind feature flag
Phase 4 (Rollout): staged rollout via console A/B on selected workspaces; collect visual regression diffs and cost delta
Phase 5 (Cleanup): remove temporary per-component overrides and deprecate old ad-hoc values after 2 cycles
acceptance_criteria: Design tokens published in tokens repo and available in design-tokens package
Figma spec contains light/dark examples and accessibility notes for contrast thresholds
At least 3 core components (Button, TableRow, ChartPoint) implement tokens behind feature flag
Performance test shows <=1% p50 rendering CPU delta for console list views in dense mode
E2E visual regressions labelled and triaged; no introduced accessibility contrast failures
design_notes: Temporal contrast tokens are overlays (alpha blends) rather than hard color swaps to avoid palette collisions
Kinetic elevation uses tighter blur/offsets and lower alpha than current elevations to avoid casting long shadows in dense UIs
Provide guidance for motion-reduced mode: only apply temporal-contrast-sm as a static indicator; remove kinetic shadow transitions
Include CSS custom property examples and JS token shim for environments that don't support variable shadow lists
qa_checks: Verify hover/press states in light and dark with 3 contrast simulators (low vision, high-luminance, night mode)
Validate shadow rasterization across Chromium, WebKit, and Electron windows (list views and popovers)
Run visual-regression jobs against baseline branches and confirm diffs are intentional
Accessibility audit: ensure contrast ratios for focused microstates meet AA when considered against local surfaces
